view.mapping: screen_x = (design_x - pan) * 1.875, pan in design px over 0..320. Display Mode FULL STRETCHES the 1280x720 frame to 2400x1080 (x 1.875, y 1.5); it neither letterboxes nor crops. The 2026-09-20 note here said it filled the width and cropped the height; that was retracted on 2026-09-24: the dump's flip panel at design (554,668) maps to (1039,1002) against the measured monitor point (1040,1002), where a centred crop would put it off-screen at y=1117, and all four title rows and every Custom Night control land within 4 px under the stretch.
view.measuredPan: A hold at the right edge moved the view 601 px against 600 predicted by 320 design px * (2400/1280). A 2500 ms hold at the LEFT edge moved 0 px, which measured saturation and not absence -- the view was already at its left limit. That null nearly became evidence of no pan at all (mistake register entry 12, in a new costume).
view.startsAtNote: Every game here starts the night panned fully left. That makes pan at t=0 a known constant rather than something to observe.

left.why: The source's fastest left-scroll band is design x <153. At the measured 1.875 scale, x=200 is inside that band; 310 ms clears the measured 270 ms 5/5 floor by 40 ms. The exact point has not itself been device-qualified, so the runner records it as SOURCE_DERIVED rather than promoting it to a measured coordinate.

right.why: The source's fastest right-scroll band is design x >1143. At the measured 1.875 scale, x=2200 is inside that band; 310 ms clears the measured 270 ms 5/5 floor by 40 ms. The exact point has not itself been device-qualified, so the runner records it as SOURCE_DERIVED rather than promoting it to a measured coordinate.

contactRule: 160 ms held contact, and a 270 ms floor for a pan hold (5/5, with 260 ms at 4/5 beneath it) against the 2500 ms that was being used. `adb shell input tap` is dropped phase-dependently by this engine.
whyThisFileExists: The two doors are 2779-2780 px apart in world space on a 2400 px screen, so they can never both be reachable from one view and every door press is pan-then-press. device-profile-v1's flat controlMap cannot express that; this is the first map that states an anchor kind and the pan its coordinate was read at. The separation is deliberately NOT stored: tools/device/test-control-anchor.mjs derives it from these coordinates, so the fact and the numbers cannot drift apart.
notMeasured: The exact right-door x. This table reads 2286 and plans/26's own world-x derivation reads 2285, so the separation is 2779 or 2780. Nothing here depends on which: both exceed the 2400 px screen. UNKNOWN(1px).
Camera view ids. FNaF 1's are alphanumeric and the view-id map has not been built -- UNKNOWN(unmapped-view-ids), which is also what blocks settling the Foxy `viewing <> 99` discrepancy.

Whether these coordinates hold at any Options combination other than the one in force when they were read. FNaF 1's Options carries Display Mode, Perspective Effect and Vibrations, and unlike FNaF 3 has NO Controller Size.
